testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What happens if you don't drain air tanks?

options.text: Water freezes and causes brake failure.
Too much air builds up in the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water freezes and causes brake failure.
questions.explanation: Air brake tanks need to be drained regularly to remove water and oil. If water stays in the tanks, it can freeze in cold weather and stop the brakes from working.

questions.question: What should you do when leaving your vehicle unattended?

options.text: Lower all windows in the cab.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: Water and oil are often found in air brake systems. What should be done with them?

options.text: They are necessary for the system to work.
They should make up about 10 percent of the tank.

questions.explanation: Water and oil buildup can damage an air brake system. Tanks have drain valves to remove this buildup. You should drain the tanks at the end of each driving day.

questions.question: What should you do if the low air pressure warning comes on?

options.text: Test the brakes while driving and continue if they seem okay.
Keep driving with hazard lights on.

questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning comes on, stop and park your vehicle as soon as possible. You need to stop while you still have some braking power left.

questions.question: An emergency brake must be controlled by:
questions.explanation: All trucks and buses must have emergency and parking brakes. They should use mechanical force because air pressure can leak away over time.

questions.question: The air compressor is connected to the:
questions.explanation: The air compressor connects to the engine with gears or a belt. It can be cooled by air or by the engine's cooling system.

questions.question: When leaving a vehicle unattended, what should a driver do?

options.text: Only set the parking brake on slopes.
Let air out of the tires by 10 percent.

questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when you leave your vehicle unattended.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: They should not be used in cold weather.
They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
They send air to the brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: They remove water and oil from the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Compressed air usually contains water and oil. Drain valves help remove these from the tanks so they don't harm the system.

questions.question: What does it mean if the ABS light comes on while driving?

options.text: The ABS cannot work because of weather.
The ABS has just been activated.
The ABS is not working properly.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working properly.
questions.explanation: An ABS warning light means something in the Anti-Lock Braking System is not working correctly.

questions.question: A low air pressure warning signal:

options.text: Is not required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
Is optional on vehicles with air brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required on vehicles with air brakes.
questions.explanation: All vehicles with air brakes must have a low air pressure warning signal. If it goes off while driving, stop the vehicle and have the system checked.

questions.question: What do both systems in a dual air brake system share?
questions.explanation: Both systems share one air compressor. If the air compressor breaks, neither system will work properly.

questions.question: A safety valve opens at ____ pounds per square inch (psi).
questions.explanation: The safety valve protects air tanks from too much pressure. It usually opens at 150 psi.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, if one air system is very low on pressure:

options.text: None of the brakes will work.
Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
There is usually no noticeable effect.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either the front or rear brakes will not work fully.
questions.explanation: If one air system has low pressure, either the front or rear brakes will not work fully. If air pressure is too low while driving, exit the road and park as soon as possible.

questions.question: Alcohol evaporators:

options.text: Add alcohol to brake systems to prevent freezing.
Are only allowed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Add alcohol to brake systems to prevent freezing.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems use an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to prevent ice from forming, which can damage the system.

questions.question: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have:
questions.explanation: Truck tractors with air brakes made on or after March 1, 1997 must have anti-lock brakes.

questions.question: What type of force do emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air brakes have three systems: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. Emergency and parking brakes use mechanical force.

questions.question: The ____ between an air compressor and reservoir tank stops air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve sits between the air compressor and the main reservoir. It stops air from leaking out of the system if the compressor breaks.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the safe maximum leakage rate for a double combination vehicle?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the leakage rate should be no more than 3 psi in one minute. Faster leakage means the vehicle needs repairs and should not be driven.

questions.question: Brakes out of adjustment will:

options.text: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cause some brakes to overwork and fail.
questions.explanation: Brakes out of adjustment wear out faster than properly adjusted brakes. Check brake adjustment often to prevent problems.

questions.question: Friction in an S-cam brake happens when the brake shoes and linings:

options.text: Press against the outside of the brake drum.
Press against the inside of the brake drum.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press against the inside of the brake drum.
questions.explanation: Friction happens when brake shoes and linings press against the inside of the drum. This friction slows and stops the vehicle.

questions.question: In a vehicle with dual parking control valves, what can a separate air tank do?

options.text: Make the air brakes work better.
Charge the brakes on the rear trailer.

questions.explanation: A separate air tank in a vehicle with dual parking control valves can temporarily release the spring brakes. This happens when the brakes activate due to low air pressure. The driver can push the proper control to release the spring brakes for a short time. This allows the vehicle to move in an emergency.

questions.question: What do air brakes use to work?
questions.explanation: Large trucks use air brakes. An air braking system uses compressed air to operate.

questions.question: What color light shows that anti-lock brakes are not working?
questions.explanation: Vehicles with Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) have a yellow warning light. This light shows when there is a problem with the braking system.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle in one minute during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: You need to know the safe air loss rate for your vehicle. A double combination vehicle should not lose more than 4 psi of air in one minute during an applied leakage test.

questions.question: What are alcohol evaporators?

options.text: Used to add alcohol into air brake systems
Only allowed in the northern parts of the state

questions.correctAnswerText: Used to add alcohol into air brake systems
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have alcohol evaporators. These devices add alcohol into the braking system to prevent ice from forming.
